title: SRE: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, Incident Review Standards & Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview:

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review requirements, operational tooling, and canonical runbooks. It is intended for on-call engineers, service owners, and platform teams. Follow these standards for defining, measuring, and acting on reliability objectives across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

1) SLOs & Error Budgets

- Purpose: SLOs quantify customer expectations and define error budgets that enable trade-offs between feature velocity and reliability. All production services must define at least one Availability SLO and one Latency/Quality SLO where relevant.

- Format (required fields for every SLO):
  - service_name: human-readable service (e.g., api.text.generate)
  - objective: percent (e.g., 99.95%)
  - window: rolling window (30d or 90d)
  - metric: explicit metric (e.g., success_rate, p99_latency_ms)
  - owner: service owner (team member)
  - measurement_query: Prometheus/BigQuery query used to compute SLO

- Example SLOs (canonical):
  - api.text.generate availability: objective=99.95% over 30d; metric=success_rate (HTTP 2xx requests / total requests). Allowed downtime ~21.6 minutes per 30d. Owner: infra-inference.
  - api.text.generate latency: objective=p95 < 250ms, p99 < 1000ms over 30d. Metric computed on server-side token-generation latency.
  - embedding.compute availability: objective=99.9% over 30d.

- Error budget policy (standard escalation):
  1. Burn > 20% within window: notify service owner / weekly review.
  2. Burn > 50% within window: freeze non-critical deploys, prioritize reliability PRs.
  3. Burn > 80% within window: require immediate remediation plan, exec/engineering leadership notified.
  4. Burn >= 100%: declare SLO breach — run full postmortem, implement short-term mitigation and long-term fixes.

- Measurement & Tooling:
  - All SLOs must be instrumented in the SLO dashboard (Grafana/Prometheus or BigQuery-backed dashboards).
  - Error budget burn rate should be computed daily and surfaced to the team Slack channel #slo-alerts.
  - Synthetic canaries: at least one synthetic probe per region for high-traffic services.

2) Capacity Planning

- Goals: ensure predictable throughput and headroom for peak traffic, controlled costs, and graceful degradation under overload.

- Inputs required for each capacity plan:
  - baseline RPS (30d P50), peak RPS (30d P99), 95th percentile request size (tokens), sustained concurrency, and spike factor (x multiplier to cover bursts, default 1.5).
  - model memory and vRAM per replica, per-model KV cache size, avg response tokens.

- Sizing formula (reference):
  - required_replicas = ceil( (peak_RPS * avg_latency_seconds) / (target_utilization * QPS_per_replica) )
  - target_utilization (recommended) = 60% for GPU-backed model servers to leave headroom for garbage/compaction and cold starts.

- Headroom policy:
  - Default safety headroom = 25% reserved capacity above expected peak for Hosted API. For Dedicated customers this is configurable per contract.
  - Autoscaling thresholds: scale_up when queue_length > 50 and avg_latency > p95_latency_threshold for 60s; scale_down when utilization < 40% for 10m.

- Capacity exercises & cadence:
  - Quarterly capacity review led by eng-sre with model-serving and infra teams.
  - Monthly load tests for top 10 services; results published to "capacity" dashboard.
  - Pre-major-release spike tests and canary phases for new models.

3) Reliability Initiatives (programmatic workstreams)

- Quarterly reliability themes should be selected from incident trends and SLO gaps. Examples of initiatives:
  - KV cache cold-start reduction (reduce first-token latency by 30%). Owner: serving-runtime.
  - Model-variant fallback improvements to reduce user-facing errors during overloads. Owner: eng-platform.
  - Auto-batching improvements to increase throughput per GPU by 15%. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

- Initiative governance:
  - Each initiative must have: objective, success metrics, owner, milestone plan (quarterly), and runbook/upgrades.

4) Incident Review Standards

- Severity definitions (SRE standard):
  - Sev 1: Major outage with broad customer impact or data loss. Immediate page to on-call and exec.
  - Sev 2: Partial outage or severe degradation for a subset of customers/features.
  - Sev 3: Minor impact, degraded experience, limited scope.

- Required incident response steps:
  1. Triage & page: on-call takes ownership within 5 minutes for Sev1/2.
  2. Declare incident channel (Slack) and create incident ticket (Jira/INC-).
  3. Post initial incident summary within 30 minutes (impact, mitigation in progress, owner).
  4. Track timeline of detection, mitigation, and recovery in the incident doc.
  5. Blameless postmortem: publish within 7 business days for Sev1 and within 14 business days for Sev2.

- Postmortem template (must be present as top-level sections):
  - Title, incident id, severity, summary (1–2 sentences).
  - Impact and scope (customers affected, downtime, incorrect outputs).
  - Detection and timeline (timestamps in UTC).
  - Root cause analysis (technical chain of events).
  - Short-term mitigation(s) taken.
  - Long-term action items (owner, due date, verification steps).
  - Lessons learned and follow-up review date.

- RCA requirements:
  - Include logs, traces, and metric graphs supporting the root cause.
  - Reference related IDs and runbooks used.
  - Link to code/PRs for fixes.

5) Operational Tooling & Dashboards

- Minimum dashboards per service:
  - SLO Dashboard: success_rate, error_budget_remaining, burn_rate, recent SLO history.
  - Latency Dashboard: p50/p95/p99, request size distribution, cold-start rate.
  - Capacity Dashboard: replica_count, GPU_utilization, queue_length, avg_inflight_requests, memory_pressure.
  - Error Dashboard: 5xx error breakdowns, model-timeouts, downstream failures.

- Standard alerts (examples):
  - High error rate: alert if 5xx_rate > 0.5% for 5m AND traffic > 100rps.
  - Latency degradation: alert if p99_latency > 1200ms for 3m.
  - Error budget burn: alert if burn_rate > 0.1/day (configurable per SLO).
  - Capacity pressure: alert if GPU_utilization > 90% for 5m or queue_length > 200 for 2m.

- Tool integrations: Slack for paging, PagerDuty for rotations/escallation, Jira for incident tracking, BigQuery for long-term metrics.

6) Canonical Runbooks (index)

- Required runbooks and owners (must be maintained in eng-sre/runbooks):
  - service-high-error-rate (owner: service team)
  - model-fallback-triggered (owner: serving-runtime)
  - gpu-node-oom (owner: infra-gpu)
  - degraded-kv-cache (owner: serving-runtime)
  - deploy-rollback-procedure (owner: eng-platform)

- Example runbook: service-high-error-rate (api.text.generate)
  - Purpose: triage and mitigate high 5xx rate for text.generate.
  - Pager flow: on-call -> initial triage -> declare incident if Sev2/Sev1.
  - Triage steps:
    1. Confirm alert in Grafana and cross-check Prometheus query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-text",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-text"}[5m]))
    2. Identify error class: model timeouts vs HTTP proxy vs downstream (db) by checking logs (ELK query examples included).
    3. If model timeouts and queue_length > threshold: temporarily increase replicas (scale_up) or route traffic to warm pool / fallback model variant.
    4. If proxy errors: roll back recent deploy (use deploy-rollback-procedure) and contact platform on-call.
    5. Post incident: run postmortem template and attach timeline + supporting traces.

- Example runbook: gpu-node-oom
  - Detection: node OOM alerts, pod evictions, GPU memory pressure > 95%.
  - Immediate actions:
    1. Mark node unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node>
    2. Evict non-critical pods to restore node stability.
    3. If multiple nodes affected: scale up spare capacity and route traffic away from affected AZ.
    4. Collect dmesg, kubelet, and nvidia-driver logs and attach to incident ticket.
  - Long-term: investigate memory leak in model runtime or adjust per-replica memory limits.

Governance & Maintenance:

- Ownership: service owners must review SLOs and runbooks quarterly and after any Sev2/Sev1. Eng-SRE will perform an annual audit of all SLOs and capacity plans.
- Documentation: runbooks must be in the eng-sre Confluence area and linked from the service README.
- Enforcement: teams missing SLO instrumentation or runbooks will be flagged in the quarterly reliability review and required to remediate within one quarter.

Appendix: Quick references

- Prometheus example query for availability: 
  (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-text",status=~"2.."}[30d])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-text"}[30d])))

- Contact matrix:
  - Primary on-call: infra-inference on-call schedule (PagerDuty)
  - Secondary: eng-platform on-call
  - Escalation to manager/exec for Sev1 within 15 minutes.

End of document. This page is normative: follow these standards when defining SLOs, planning capacity, executing incident reviews, and authoring runbooks.
